back: A place where tree seedlings are raised and cared for until they are ready to plant out.
Transferring young seedlings from a seedbed into individual pots or tubes.
Gradually reducing water and shade before planting out so seedlings survive field conditions.
Near water, well drained, sheltered but not under big trees, secure and fenced, good soil, not a frost hollow.
Thinning removes whole trees to give space; pruning removes lower branches for knot-free timber and fire control.
Replacing seedlings that die after planting out.
Growing trees together with crops and/or livestock on the same land for mutual benefit.
Alley cropping, boundary planting, windbreaks, improved fallows, fodder banks, scattered trees, woodlots.
Trees/ha = 10,000 ÷ (row spacing in m × in-row spacing in m).
